source.title: Kraken Robotics reports Q2 2026 financial results
source.locator: August 27, 2026; financial highlights and new orders
source.summary: Quarterly results distinguish standalone Kraken from post-July acquisition scope and report a new XL-UUV battery supply agreement.

leads.evidenceLocator: August 27, 2026; financial highlights and new orders
followUpQuestions: Which RMDS deliverables and support obligations remain after the June 2026 amendment, and does that amendment relate to the Q2 integration-project revenue reversal?
For the proposed vessel and survey speed, what real-time imagery, post-processing latency, storage and launch/recovery configuration will the supplied KATFISH system deliver?
reviewWarnings: The CanadaBuys C$12,154,000.20 reduction on W8472-105270/001/QF is not explicitly linked by the reviewed documents to Kraken's C$1.5 million Q2 revenue reversal; do not equate the two amounts or infer cancellation.
SeaPower brochure specifies 2 kWh minimum while the current product page says 1.8 kWh; confirm the offered module and certification package rather than treating the ranges as interchangeable.
The XL-UUV battery customer is unnamed, and announced orders, master supply agreements and management guidance do not establish delivered revenue or future production throughput.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: Kraken Q2 newsroom retrieval resolved the August 27 standalone reporting boundary, XL-UUV agreement and revenue reversal; direct Python access returned 403 but the web reader recovered the document.
KATFISH two-page fact sheet recovered resolution modes, 300 m depth, 4–10 knot envelope, data formats and topside storage; no field-performance guarantee was inferred.
SeaPower brochure recovered BMS controls and 6000 m rating; comparison with the current product page left the 2 kWh versus 1.8 kWh minimum as a configuration question.
Kraken interim financial statements Note 22 resolved cash, term-debt and equity components of the Covelya transaction; acquisition accounting was still provisional when issued.
Kraken Q2 MD&A page 7 resolved the C$6.911 million supplier-arbitration provision into royalty, interest and legal-cost estimates; no shutdown or final court judgment was established.

CanadaBuys web fetch was blocked; normal browser recovery in French and English verified the June 11 amendment of C$-12,154,000.20 and December 29, 2028 expiry, without establishing a link to the C$1.5 million revenue reversal.
DND original award separated the RMDS acquisition and support contracts and Canadian recipient; its expected 2025 operation date was not promoted to current acceptance.
Kraken official contact page verified Mount Pearl and Dartmouth addresses plus head-office phone; KATFISH fact sheet supplied the public sales email.
Kraken April results confirmed announced Nova Scotia facility completion; no current measured throughput or available production slots were published in the inspected material.
Targeted defence-newsletter discovery found an August 20 CDR acquisition lead; public statements and filings supplied the evidence, and no newsletter wording entered public proposed fields.

leads.refreshSummary: Assess Kraken Robotics as a KATFISH towing and topside processing supplier alongside its Canadian RMDS integration role: Department of National Defence buyer evidence and the August 27 results change the delivery-scope and financial questions worth asking. The operating context and current activity changes are fully proposed for human review.

source.title: COVE and Communitech announce dual-use collaboration
source.locator: September 2, 2026; opening, collaboration and planned Waterloo Tech Week event
source.summary: COVE announces collaboration connecting Atlantic testing and Waterloo technology communities, with a future event rather than completed adoption outcomes.

leads.evidenceLocator: September 2, 2026; opening, collaboration and planned Waterloo Tech Week event

aliases: Centre for Ocean Ventures and Entrepreneurship

followUpQuestions: Which Stella Maris setup, interfaces, test window and project-specific funding conditions fit the proposed sensor trial?
Can this proposed sensor participate in the DRDC Sea Tracker experimentation pathway, and who authorizes the trial and data access?
reviewWarnings: The September 14–18 Waterloo Tech Week activity is planned; the September 2 collaboration does not establish completed adoption, funding or procurement outcomes.

Stella Maris funding is conditional and project-specific; published material does not give a tariff, confirmed slot, interface acceptance or classification/security approval for a particular deployment.
Sea Tracker is supplied by Ultra Maritime for DRDC experimentation; COVE collaboration does not establish ownership of the sonar product or unrestricted third-party access to defence trials.
The old Start-Up Yard program URL returns 404 and the current service index labels Incubators coming soon; verify current intake before routing a company to the historical participation record.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: COVE September 2 announcement resolved the Communitech collaboration and planned September 14–18 event; targeted counterpart search yielded no separate completion evidence.

COVE Stella Maris detailed service page recovered subsea, dockside, shoreside and data access plus project enquiry fields; the linked extra resource failed, while the detailed page answered the access mechanics.

DND March 12 DIANA account independently verified COVE Dartmouth curriculum delivery and competitive selection; the French counterpart confirmed the same facts rather than adding independent evidence.
COVE official DIANA page established accelerator operator status and facilities/mentorship access; dynamic network-size counts were omitted because dated sources describe different totals.
Ultra Maritime December 3 Sea Tracker announcement established supplier-to-DRDC experimentation roles and named COVE/ACOA collaboration; it did not establish unrestricted public test access.

COVE December 4 at-sea announcement recorded C$9,690,773 federal project funding; targeted government funding search did not recover a separate award breakdown, so it remains attributed project funding.
COVE official contact page verified 27 Parker Street, Dartmouth, phone and program enquiry; email was obscured and is left null.
COVE current service index labels Incubators coming soon; the former Start-Up Yard URL returned 404 and historical cohort search did not establish a current open intake or closure.
